{"classStructure":["PreviewController: HTTP handler for GET /api/v1/urls/{code}/preview; validates the short code exists, delegates to PreviewService, maps results to HTTP responses (200, 404, 503)","PreviewService: Orchestrates preview retrieval; checks PreviewCache first, falls back to MetadataFetcher, writes results back to cache, enforces overall SLA timeout","MetadataFetcher: Performs the external HTTP GET against the resolved target URL, parses <title> and <meta name='description'> from the HTML head, respects a configurable per-fetch timeout and follows up to N redirects","PreviewCache: Read/write abstraction over a Redis (or in-process fallback) store; keys on short code; stores serialized PreviewDocument with a configurable TTL","PreviewDocument: Value object / entity holding: shortCode (string), targetUrl (string), title (string|null), description (string|null), fetchedAt (ISO-8601), cacheExpiresAt (ISO-8601)","UrlRepository (existing, modified): Add lookupByCode(code) → UrlRecord|null used by PreviewService to resolve the target URL and confirm the code exists","PreviewConfig: Configuration value object exposing fetchTimeoutMs (default 3000), cacheTimeoutMs (default 3000), cacheTtlSeconds (default 86400), maxRedirects (default 5)"],"apiContract":"paths:
  /api/v1/urls/{code}/preview:
    get:
      summary: Return cached title and description for the target URL of a short code
      parameters:
        - name: code
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            example: aB3xQ
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Preview metadata (may be partial if title or description absent on target page)
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                required: [shortCode, targetUrl, fetchedAt]
                properties:
                  shortCode:
                    type: string
                    example: aB3xQ
                  targetUrl:
                    type: string
                    format: uri
                    example: https://example.com/some/article
                  title:
                    type: string
                    nullable: true
                    example: Example Domain
                  description:
                    type: string
                    nullable: true
                    example: An example article about something
                  fetchedAt:
                    type: string
                    format: date-time
                  cacheExpiresAt:
                    type: string
                    format: date-time
        '404':
          description: Short code not found
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  error:
                    type: string
                    example: Short code 'aB3xQ' not found
        '503':
          description: External fetch timed out or failed; no cached preview available
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  error:
                    type: string
                    example: Preview unavailable: upstream fetch timed out
                  retryAfter:
                    type: integer
                    description: Suggested seconds before retry
                    example: 30","dataModelChanges":["New Redis key schema: preview:{code} → JSON-serialised PreviewDocument; TTL set to cacheTtlSeconds (default 86400 s); atomic SET NX used on first write to prevent stampede","New RDBMS table 'url_previews' (optional persistent fallback): columns: short_code VARCHAR PK, target_url TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NULL, description TEXT NULL, fetched_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, cache_expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL; index on cache_expires_at for background eviction jobs","No changes to existing 'urls' / 'short_links' table schema; UrlRepository gains a read-only lookupByCode query against that existing table"],"chosenApproach":"Cache-aside with Redis and a bounded external fetch: PreviewController receives the request and calls PreviewService. PreviewService first calls PreviewCache.get(code); on a cache hit it returns the stored PreviewDocument immediately. On a cache miss it calls UrlRepository.lookupByCode(code) — returning 404 if absent — then calls MetadataFetcher.fetch(targetUrl) wrapped in a timeout (fetchTimeoutMs). On success the document is written to PreviewCache with a TTL and returned as a 200. On timeout/network failure with no cached data a 503 is returned; if a stale cached entry exists it is returned with a staleness flag rather than a 503 ('stale-while-revalidate' semantics). All timeout values and the cache TTL are externalised in PreviewConfig so they can be tuned without a code change. MetadataFetcher only downloads the HTML head section (HTTP Range or stream-and-abort after </head>) to minimise bandwidth. This approach keeps latency predictable, protects the service from slow external sites, and avoids redundant fetches for popular codes.","rejectedAlternatives":[{"alternative":"Eager pre-fetch at shortening time: when a new short URL is created, immediately fetch and store the preview metadata in the background","reason":"Adds latency/complexity to the URL-creation critical path and wastes resources for codes that are never previewed. It also does not handle codes created before this feature ships, requiring a backfill job. Cache-aside fetches on demand and only for codes that actually receive preview requests."},{"alternative":"No caching — always fetch from the target URL on each preview request","reason":"Makes response time entirely dependent on external site performance, violates the stated requirement for caching, risks rate-limiting or blocking by target hosts under even moderate traffic, and exposes the service to SSRF amplification without the blast-radius reduction that a cached path provides."},{"alternative":"Use a third-party link-preview SaaS API (e.g. LinkPreview.net) instead of in-house MetadataFetcher","reason":"Introduces an external runtime dependency and potential data-privacy concerns (all target URLs are sent to a third party).
